title: Gradient of a linear graph as the ratio of vertical change to horizontal change
summary: Calculate and interpret positive, negative, zero and fractional gradients from points, graphs and contexts.
objectives: Calculate gradient from vertical and horizontal changes.
Find gradient from two coordinates using a consistent subtraction order.
Use equal gradients to solve problems involving parallel or collinear lines.

blocks.text: Gradient measures how y changes as x increases. Use the same point order in the numerator and denominator. A line rising from left to right has positive gradient, a falling line has negative gradient, and a horizontal line has gradient zero.
Parallel non-vertical lines have equal gradients. Collinear points also give the same gradient whichever pair is chosen.

sections.title: Gradient from two points

prompt.text: Find the gradient of the line through (-2, 7) and (4, -5).

content.text: Divide vertical change by horizontal change.

sections.verification_note: The negative gradient agrees with the line falling as x increases.

prompt.text: A line rises 15 units while moving 5 units to the right. Find its gradient.

blocks.text: Subtract coordinates in a consistent order, divide vertical change by horizontal change, and use the sign to interpret the line's direction.
